A fresh R-546 replay passes 32/32; its stored integrated artifact differs only in the Lean registry pin 68debd5579b3ce0980428f4aab6490a5b534f378b659741b01d0ef8c840113af versus current d2ec6c2a75e373bd369ce9478af1df1e7c6633acf5285db87432de137542daa4. decision_reason: This correction separates two historical provenance drifts from the mathematical route. The fixed-n theorem and the exact two-term reduction remain usable inputs; the missing anchored-n D_n route and owner packet remain the genuine frontier.
boundary: PAH-001, PAH-OMC-018/020, the original functions, rates, labelled Gibbs state, external stochastic Markov time, finite carrier, post-j correlation c_n and j-before-anchored-n order remain fixed. No new comparison map, carrier, counterterm, state, rate, regulator or physical interpretation is introduced.
verification_summary: R-514 fixed-n proof integrated PASS; R-546 fresh two-term integrated replay PASS 32/32. The two failing historical wrapper checks are isolated to temporal-work and Lean-registry hash drift, not to the fixed-n theorem or the two-term inequality.
next_action: Use R-514 and R-546 only as fixed-n and logical reduction inputs. Keep the full goal active and reopen the anchored-n proof only when a complete source-authorized R-536 form/path packet supplies D_n(T)->0 and the common-space/target fields.

non_claims: This correction does not prove anchored-n convergence, R-512 minimal-form identification or the full PAH-OMC-020 objective.

The wrapper failures are provenance/environment issues, not mathematical counterexamples.
